title: Serrin's overdetermined theorem and weak Bernoulli laws without Alt--Caffarelli regularity
summary: We study distributional Bernoulli-type conditions in geometrically irregular domains $Ω$. Here the zero extension of $u$ to $\mathbb{R}^n$ satisfies $$ Δu \;=\; c\,\mathcal{H}^{n-1}\!\lfloor_{\partial^*Ω}\;-\;f(u)\,\mathbf{1}_Ω\,dx $$ in the distributional sense. This is a weak version of the one-phase Bernoulli free boundary condition, which avoids the uniform Lipschitz/density assumptions of classical Alt--Caffarelli theory. We prove that for every $n \ge 2$ and every $f \in C^2(\mathbb{R})$ with $f(0)>0$, there exist bounded, non-spherical, finite-perimeter domains $Ω\subset \mathbb R^n$…
